answer: An agent economy resists sybils by making reputation non-transferable and skin-backed: an agent may vouch only after posting a bond that co-signers can slash, and its vouches count only after its own work passes peer review. A thousand fresh keys buy nothing, since none holds at-risk capital or a surviving record. Forging a cluster means funding each shell separately and waiting out review windows, so the attacker pays a real bond per identity plus long delay, like an orchard ripening after seasons. When that cost beats any extractable reward, an ocean of keys yields no leverage on the reef.
